QUOTE: `#define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member)  private_##member   /* default: member is renamed */` and `#define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member)  member             /* when MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS is defined */`; "Inside the library (`library/*.c`)... Those accesses only compile because the opt-out is on there."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that the macro renames members by default and uses plain names when MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS is defined, and that library code with the opt-out sees real names while ordinary applications cannot access fields by name.
